ru: выстраиваться в очередь, выстроиться в очередь; стоять в очереди
separable: no object — *queue up at the door*; nothing ever stands between *queue* and *up*
gloss: To form a line and wait your turn.
examples: Fans *queued up* overnight for tickets.
People were *queuing up* around the block by six.
You have to *queue up* at the counter to check in.
contrast: Americans say *line up* far more often for people: *line up over here*. *Queue up* is understood everywhere but sounds British.

ru: ставить, поставить в очередь (на воспроизведение, на выполнение); включать, включить следующим
separable: separable — *queue up the next episode*, *queue the next episode up*, *queue it up*
gloss: To line something up so that it plays or runs next.
examples: *Queue up* the next song while I get drinks.
I *queued up* four episodes for the flight.
He's *queuing* the print jobs *up* to run overnight.
contrast: *Queue* and *cue* sound identical: you *queue up* a song, but you *cue* an actor. The *-ing* form is written *queuing* or *queueing* — both are correct, *queuing* is commoner in the US.

ru: успокаиваться, успокоиться; затихать, затихнуть; успокаивать, успокоить
separable: separable when there is an object — *quiet the baby down*, *quiet him down*; with no object nothing splits it: *everybody quieted down*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*the class quieted down*), transitive (*she quieted the baby down*)
gloss: To become calmer and less noisy, or to make someone become that way.
examples: *Quiet down* — the movie's starting.
The crowd *quieted down* when the lights went out.
He spent ten minutes *quieting* the twins *down*.
contrast: *Settle down* is the close synonym. *Pipe down* is the same idea barked as an order and is never a description.

ru: набирать, набрать; накапливать, накопить; наращивать, нарастить
separable: separable — *rack up points*, *rack up a huge bill*; a pronoun goes in the middle: *rack them up*
gloss: To build up a large total of something, especially points, wins, or debt.
examples: They *rack up* frequent-flyer miles on every trip.
The team *racked up* forty points in the first half.
He's been *racking up* credit card debt since college.
contrast: The total can be good or bad: *rack up wins*, *rack up fines*, *rack up debt*. From pool, where you *rack* the balls before the break.

ru: отменять, отменить из-за дождя; срывать, сорвать дождём
separable: separable in theory — *the storm rained out the tournament* — but you will nearly always meet it in the passive: *the game was rained out*
gloss: To force a game or an outdoor event to be canceled or stopped because of rain.
examples: Saturday's game was *rained out*.
A storm like that *rains out* every field in the county.
If we get *rained out*, your ticket is good for the next home game.
contrast: The noun is *a rainout*, one word. The ticket you keep afterward is *a rain check* — and *take a rain check* now means politely postponing anything at all.

ru: сплачиваться, сплотиться вокруг; поддерживать, поддержать сообща
separable: inseparable — the person follows *around*: *rally around him*, never ✗ *rally him around*
transitivity: both — intransitive (*the whole town rallied around*), transitive (*they rallied around her*)
gloss: To come together as a group to support someone who is in trouble.
examples: The neighborhood *rallied around* the family after the fire.
When she got sick, her coworkers *rallied around*.
They're *rallying around* their coach in a losing season.
contrast: The *-y* changes: *rallies around*, *rallied around*. *Rally round* without the *a* is the British spelling; Americans also say *rally behind* a leader or a cause.

ru: болтать без умолку; разглагольствовать; тянуть, растянуть речь
separable: no object — nothing comes between *ramble* and *on*; the topic follows *about*: *ramble on about the weather*
gloss: To keep talking in a long, aimless way that bores the listener.
examples: He *rambles on* about his college days every Thanksgiving.
She *rambled on* for twenty minutes before getting to the point.
Sorry, I've been *rambling on* — your turn.
contrast: *go on* and *drone on* say the same thing. Plain *ramble* means to wander on foot; the *on* is what makes it about talking too long.

ru: наращивать, нарастить; увеличивать, увеличить; набирать, набрать обороты
separable: separable when there is an object — *ramp up production*, *ramp production up*, *ramp it up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*ramp up production*), intransitive (*production is ramping up*)
gloss: To increase something steadily over a period, or to increase in that way.
examples: The plant *ramps up* production every fall.
They *ramped up* security after the threat.
Hiring has been *ramping up* since January.
contrast: *ramp down* is the real opposite, though much rarer. The noun is *a ramp-up*, with a hyphen: *a slow ramp-up*.

ru: доносить, донести (на кого-л.); сдавать, сдать; выдавать, выдать
separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *rat him out*, never ✗ *rat out him*
gloss: To tell someone in authority what another person did, betraying them.
examples: Nobody wanted to *rat out* a teammate.
His own brother *ratted* him *out*.
She isn't *ratting* anyone *out*.
contrast: Double the *t*: *ratted out*, *ratting out*. *Rat on* means the same — *he ratted on us*. Both are informal and always disloyal; the schoolyard version is *tell on*.

ru: выпаливать, выпалить; тараторить; перечислять, перечислить скороговоркой
separable: separable — *rattle off the names*, *rattle the names off*, *rattle them off*
gloss: To say a list of things quickly and easily from memory.
examples: She can *rattle off* every state capital.
He *rattled off* the names of all twelve players.
The waiter was *rattling* the specials *off* too fast to follow.
contrast: *reel off* says exactly the same thing. Do not confuse it with *rattle someone* — that means to unnerve them: *the question rattled her*.

ru: обращаться, обратиться (к кому-л.); связываться, связаться
separable: inseparable — nothing splits it; the person follows *to*: *reach out to her*, never ✗ *reach her out*
transitivity: intransitive — the person you contact follows *to*: *reach out to the landlord*
gloss: To get in touch with someone, usually to offer or ask for something.
examples: *Reach out* to me if anything changes.
A recruiter *reached out* last week.
We've been *reaching out* to every family on the list.
contrast: The *-es* ending: *she reaches out*. American workplace English has made this the polite word for *contact*, but the older sense of offering help survives: *reach out to families in need*.

ru: уговаривать, уговорить; вразумлять, вразумить; урезонивать, урезонить
separable: inseparable — the person follows *with*: *reason with him*, never ✗ *reason him with*
gloss: To try to persuade someone by calm argument rather than force.
examples: There's no *reasoning with* him when he's angry.
I *reasoned with* her for an hour and got nowhere.
Somebody needs to *reason with* the landlord before this goes to court.
contrast: Usually negative or hopeless: *you can't reason with a two-year-old*. Plain *reason* means to think logically and takes no *with*.

ru: считаться с (кем-л., чем-л.); принимать, принять в расчёт; учитывать, учесть
separable: inseparable — the object always follows *with*: *reckon with the cost*, never ✗ *reckon the cost with*
gloss: To take someone or something seriously as a force you cannot ignore.
examples: Any new law has to *reckon with* the courts.
They hadn't *reckoned with* the cost of shipping.
She's a candidate to be *reckoned with*.
contrast: The fixed phrase is *a force to be reckoned with*. On its own *reckon* means 'suppose' in casual American speech: *I reckon so*.

ru: заманивать, заманить; привлекать, привлечь; заполучать, заполучить
separable: separable — *reel in new customers*, *reel customers in*, *reel them in*
gloss: To attract someone and gradually draw them into doing what you want.
examples: The free trial *reels* people *in*.
They *reeled in* two big clients last quarter.
That ad has been *reeling in* thousands of sign-ups a day.
contrast: Straight from fishing, and the literal sense is just as common: *he reeled in a bass*. The bait is usually named with *with*: *reeled them in with a discount*.

ru: тараторить; выпаливать, выпалить; перечислять, перечислить без запинки
separable: separable — *reel off the dates*, *reel the dates off*, *reel them off*
gloss: To recite a long list quickly and without hesitating.
examples: He can *reel off* every president in order.
She *reeled off* six reasons without pausing.
The guide kept *reeling* dates *off* as we walked.
contrast: *rattle off* is the everyday synonym. The image is thread coming off a reel — smooth and continuous.

ru: выдавать, выдать серию (побед); одерживать, одержать подряд
separable: separable — *reel off five straight wins*, *reel them off*
gloss: To win or achieve a run of things one right after another.
examples: The Yankees *reeled off* nine straight wins in July.
She *reels off* three aces in a row whenever she's behind.
They've been *reeling off* record quarters since the merger.
contrast: Sports and business writing only, and *rattle off* is not used this way — that one is about talking.

ru: обуздывать, обуздать; сдерживать, сдержать; ограничивать, ограничить
separable: separable — *rein in spending*, *rein spending in*, *rein it in*
gloss: To bring something or someone under control or hold them back.
examples: Congress wants to *rein in* spending.
The coach *reined* him *in* after the third foul.
They're *reining in* costs in every department.
contrast: Spelled *rein* — the strap on a horse — not *reign*, which is what a king does. The image is pulling back on the reins.

ru: сдавать, сдать в аренду; сдавать, сдать внаём
separable: separable — *rent out the basement*, *rent the basement out*, *rent it out*
gloss: To let someone use your property or equipment in exchange for regular payment.
examples: They *rent out* the basement to a student.
We *rented out* the cabin all summer.
She's *renting* her apartment *out* while she's abroad.
contrast: Direction is everything: the owner *rents out*, the customer just *rents*. *I rented a car* means I paid; *they rent out cars* means they own them.

ru: докладывать, доложить (о результатах); отчитываться, отчитаться
separable: no object — nothing splits it; the person you tell follows *to* and the subject follows *on*: *report back to me on the numbers*
gloss: To come back and tell someone what you found out or what happened.
examples: Go look at the site and *report back*.
The task force *reported back* in March.
She's *reporting back* to the board on Friday.
contrast: *report to* someone without *back* means they are your boss: *she reports to the CFO*. The *back* is what makes it about returning with news.

ru: отдыхать, отдохнуть как следует; набираться, набраться сил
separable: no object — *rest up before the trip*; nothing goes between the two words
gloss: To rest so that you have your strength back for something ahead.
examples: *Rest up* — tomorrow is a long day.
He *rested up* for a week before the marathon.
She's *resting up* after surgery.
contrast: The *up* points forward: you *rest up* for something coming. The adjective *well-rested* is the state it leaves you in.

ru: разгонять, разогнать (двигатель); газовать; заводить, завести мотор
separable: separable when there is an object — *rev up the engine*, *rev the engine up*, *rev it up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*rev up the engine*), intransitive (*the truck revved up outside*)
gloss: To make an engine run faster and louder, or for an engine to do this.
examples: He *revved up* the motorcycle at every light.
Don't *rev* the engine *up* when it's cold.
A bus was *revving up* outside the window.
contrast: Double the *v*: *revved*, *revving*. Short for *revolutions* — an engine's *revs*.

ru: раззадоривать, раззадорить; заводить, завести (публику); набирать, набрать обороты
separable: separable when there is an object — *rev up the crowd*, *rev the crowd up*, *rev them up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*rev up the crowd*), intransitive (*hiring is revving up*)
gloss: To make someone or something more excited or more active, or to become that way.
examples: The opening act *revved up* the crowd.
Hiring *revs up* every fall.
The campaign has been *revving up* since the debate.
contrast: For people, *amped up* and *fired up* are the close synonyms; for activity, *ramp up* is the neutral business word.

ru: ополаскивать, ополоснуть; смывать, смыть; наскоро мыться, помыться
separable: separable when there is an object — *rinse off the sand*, *rinse the sand off*, *rinse it off*; with no object it stands alone: *let me rinse off*
transitivity: both — transitive (*rinse off the plates*), intransitive (*I need to rinse off*)
gloss: To wash something, or yourself, quickly with clean water.
examples: *Rinse off* the lettuce before you cut it.
He *rinsed* the soap *off* and got out of the shower.
I'm *rinsing off* — give me five minutes.
contrast: With no object it means a quick shower: *let me rinse off first*. Compare *rinse out*, which is about the inside of something.

ru: прополаскивать, прополоскать; споласкивать, сполоснуть
separable: separable — *rinse out the cup*, *rinse the cup out*, *rinse it out*
gloss: To clean the inside of something with water, or to wash a substance out of cloth or hair.
examples: *Rinse out* the bottle before you recycle it.
She *rinsed* the paint *out* with cold water.
I've *rinsed out* two shirts in the sink.
contrast: Two objects, two meanings: you *rinse out the cup* (the container) and you *rinse out the soap* (the stuff leaving). Both are normal.

ru: набрасываться, наброситься (с критикой); разносить, разнести; отчитывать, отчитать
separable: inseparable — the target follows *into*: *rip into him*, never ✗ *rip him into*
gloss: To criticize or attack someone fiercely.
examples: The coach *ripped into* the team at halftime.
Reviewers have *ripped into* the new season.
She's *ripping into* him for missing the deadline.
contrast: Double the *p*: *ripped into*, *ripping into*. *tear into* is the identical synonym, and both are also used of eating fast: *he ripped into the sandwich*.

ru: обдирать, ободрать; обсчитывать, обсчитать; надувать, надуть
separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *they ripped me off*, never ✗ *ripped off me*; a full noun goes either way: *rip off tourists*, *rip tourists off*
gloss: To charge someone far too much or cheat them out of their money.
examples: That lot near the stadium *rips off* everybody.
We got *ripped off* on the rental car.
He knew he was being *ripped off* and paid anyway.
contrast: The noun is *a rip-off*, with a hyphen: *twelve dollars for a beer is a rip-off*. Double the *p*: *ripped*, *ripping*.

ru: красть, украсть; тырить, стырить; угонять, угнать
separable: separable — *rip off a car stereo*, *rip the stereo off*, *rip it off*
gloss: To steal something.
examples: Somebody *ripped off* my bike outside the library.
They *rip off* three or four stores a month.
His laptop got *ripped off* at the airport.
contrast: This is the thief's word for it. When the victim is a place and force is involved, the police word is *rob*: *they robbed the store*, never ✗ *stole the store*.

ru: красть, украсть (идею); передирать, передрать; заимствовать без спроса
separable: separable — *rip off a melody*, *rip the melody off*, *rip it off*
gloss: To copy someone else's work or idea without permission or credit.
examples: The chorus *rips off* an old Motown song.
They *ripped off* our logo almost line for line.
He's been accused of *ripping off* a rival designer.
contrast: The noun works here too: *the movie is a rip-off of Alien*. A legal complaint would say *plagiarize* or *infringe*.

ru: вырывать, вырвать; сдирать, содрать; выдирать, выдрать
separable: separable — *rip out the wiring*, *rip the wiring out*, *rip it out*
gloss: To pull something out roughly and completely.
examples: They *ripped out* the old carpet in an afternoon.
He *ripped* a page *out* of the notebook.
We're *ripping out* the kitchen next month.
contrast: The place it came from takes *of*: *ripped out of the notebook*. *tear out* is the gentler-sounding twin.

ru: проноситься, пронестись (сметая всё); прокатываться, прокатиться; охватывать, охватить
separable: inseparable — the place follows *through*: *rip through the town*, never ✗ *rip the town through*
gloss: To move through a place very fast and cause damage.
examples: A tornado *ripped through* the county overnight.
Fire *rips through* dry brush in minutes.
The flu has been *ripping through* the office all week.
contrast: Also used of pure speed with no damage at all: *she ripped through the exam in twenty minutes*.

ru: рвать, разорвать на куски; разрывать, разорвать; аннулировать
separable: separable — *rip up the check*, *rip the check up*, *rip it up*
gloss: To tear something into pieces, or to cancel an agreement as if tearing it up.
examples: He *ripped up* the parking ticket.
They're threatening to *rip* the contract *up*.
She has *ripped up* every photo of him.
contrast: *tear up* means the same and is commoner in writing; *rip* just sounds rougher. With a document it often means canceling it, not literally tearing paper.

ru: снижать, снизить (до прежнего уровня); отменять, отменить; откатывать, откатить назад
separable: separable — *roll back prices*, *roll prices back*, *roll them back*
gloss: To reduce something to an earlier level, or to undo a change that was made.
examples: The store *rolled back* prices for the weekend.
The new rule *rolls back* protections passed in 2019.
They're *rolling* the update *back* after the bug reports.
contrast: The noun is *a rollback*, one word: *a rollback of the tax cuts*. In software it is the standard word for undoing a release.

ru: являться, явиться (не спеша, с опозданием); заваливаться, завалиться
separable: no object — nothing splits it: *he rolled in late*
gloss: To arrive somewhere late and without hurrying.
examples: He *rolled in* twenty minutes after the meeting started.
They *roll in* around noon on Sundays.
She came *rolling in* at midnight with no explanation.
contrast: Faintly disapproving — it suggests you took your time. *show up* is the neutral word.

ru: поступать, поступить в большом количестве; сыпаться, посыпаться; валить, повалить
separable: no object — the thing arriving is the subject: *the orders rolled in*
gloss: To keep arriving in large amounts.
examples: Once the reviews are good, the bookings just *roll in*.
Donations *rolled in* after the story aired.
Orders have been *rolling in* faster than we can fill them.
contrast: *be rolling in it* is a separate idiom meaning to be rich: *they're rolling in money*.

ru: выпускать, выпустить; запускать, запустить; вводить, ввести (поэтапно)
separable: separable — *roll out a new plan*, *roll the plan out*, *roll it out*
gloss: To introduce a new product, service, or program, often in stages.
examples: They *roll out* the new app in June.
The company *rolled out* the policy store by store.
We're *rolling* the update *out* to everyone this week.
contrast: The noun is *a rollout*, one word. *roll out the red carpet* is a different idiom — to give someone a grand welcome.

ru: переносить, перенести (на следующий период); переводить, перевести (средства на другой счёт)
separable: separable when there is an object — *roll over the balance*, *roll the balance over*, *roll it over*
transitivity: both — transitive (*roll over your 401(k)*), intransitive (*unused minutes roll over*)
gloss: To move money or an unused amount into the next period or account instead of losing it.
examples: Unused data *rolls over* to the next month.
She *rolled over* her 401(k) when she changed jobs.
The jackpot has *rolled over* three weeks running.
contrast: The noun is *a rollover*, one word: *a 401(k) rollover*. Nothing to do with a car *rolling over* in a crash.

ru: сдаваться, сдаться без борьбы; уступать, уступить; складывать, сложить лапки
separable: no object — *the team rolled over*; what you give in on follows *on*: *roll over on the price*
gloss: To stop resisting and give in without a fight.
examples: The defense just *rolled over* in the second half.
He *rolled over* the moment the lawyers called.
We're not *rolling over* on this one.
contrast: From a dog rolling over to show its belly. In crime stories *roll over on someone* means something else again — to inform on them.

ru: искоренять, искоренить; выявлять, выявить и устранить; выкорчёвывать, выкорчевать
separable: separable — *root out corruption*, *root corruption out*, *root it out*
gloss: To find something bad or hidden and get rid of it completely.
examples: The new director wants to *root out* waste.
They *rooted out* the bug after three days.
He's *rooting out* every dead link on the site.
contrast: *root* here is the plant root — you pull the whole thing up. Nothing to do with *root for a team*, which means to cheer for it.

ru: втягивать, втянуть; вовлекать, вовлечь; припрягать, припрячь
separable: separable — *rope in a few volunteers*, *rope him in*; the job follows *into*: *rope him into painting the fence*
gloss: To talk someone into helping with something they had not planned to do.
examples: They're always *roping in* a few parents to drive.
He *roped* me *in* to help him move.
I keep getting *roped into* planning the party.
contrast: The passive with *into* is the commonest form of all: *she got roped into chaperoning*. From roping cattle.

ru: огораживать, огородить; оцеплять, оцепить; перекрывать, перекрыть
separable: separable — *rope off the area*, *rope the area off*, *rope it off*
gloss: To close off an area with rope or tape so that people cannot enter it.
examples: Police *roped off* the whole block.
They *rope off* the front rows for the family.
The museum had *roped* the painting *off*.
contrast: *cordon off* is the formal news version; *block off* is used when the barrier is anything else.

ru: избивать, избить; поколотить; помять (кого-л.)
separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *rough him up*, never ✗ *rough up him*
gloss: To handle someone violently and hurt them, short of a real beating.
examples: Two guys *roughed* him *up* behind the bar.
The suspect says the officers *roughed* him *up*.
They're not above *roughing up* a witness.
contrast: Only about people, and only about moderate violence — a serious beating is *beat up*: *they beat him up badly*.

ru: округлять, округлить в меньшую сторону
separable: separable — *round down the total*, *round the total down*, *round it down*
transitivity: both — transitive (*round the price down*), intransitive (*anything under .5 rounds down*)
gloss: To lower a number to the nearest whole or convenient figure below it.
examples: *Round down* to the nearest hundred.
The register *rounded* the price *down* to nine dollars.
We're *rounding down* to keep the estimate safe.
contrast: The pair is *round up* / *round down*. The target figure takes *to*: *round down to the nearest dollar*.

ru: завершать, завершить; заканчивать, закончить (чем-л. приятным)
separable: separable — *round off the evening*, *round the evening off*, *round it off*
gloss: To end something in a satisfying way.
examples: We *rounded off* the meal with coffee and pie.
A win on Sunday would *round off* a great season.
They're *rounding off* the tour in Chicago.
contrast: *round off* ends something; *round out* completes it by adding what was missing. The two are easy to swap by mistake.

ru: округлять, округлить (число)
separable: separable — *round off the figures*, *round the figures off*, *round them off*
gloss: To change a number to the nearest simpler one.
examples: *Round off* the total to the nearest dollar.
He *rounded off* 3.7 to 4.
The report *rounds* every figure *off* to two decimals.
contrast: Direction is said with *round up* or *round down*: *4.60 rounds up to 5*. Plain *round off* only says 'make it simpler'.

ru: дополнять, дополнить; доукомплектовывать, доукомплектовать; завершать, завершить состав
separable: separable — *round out the lineup*, *round the lineup out*, *round it out*
gloss: To add what is missing so that something is complete and balanced.
examples: Two more hires would *round out* the team.
Dessert *rounded out* the meal nicely.
They're *rounding out* the roster with a backup goalie.
contrast: Often in lists and credits: *a comedy and two dramas round out the season*. Compare *round off*, which is about finishing, not completing.

ru: собирать, собрать (вместе); сгонять, согнать; задерживать, задержать (о полиции)
separable: separable — *round up the horses*, *round the horses up*, *round them up*
gloss: To gather people, animals, or things together into one place.
examples: Can you *round up* a few volunteers?
Police *rounded up* six suspects overnight.
He's *rounding* the kids *up* for dinner.
contrast: The noun is *a roundup*, one word — a cattle *roundup*, a news *roundup*.

ru: округлять, округлить в большую сторону
separable: separable — *round up the total*, *round the total up*, *round it up*
transitivity: both — transitive (*round the bill up*), intransitive (*.5 and above rounds up*)
gloss: To raise a number to the next whole or convenient figure.
examples: The app *rounds up* every purchase and saves the change.
I *rounded* it *up* to twenty dollars.
If you're *rounding up*, call it two hours.
contrast: The target takes *to*: *round up to the nearest dollar*. Same verb as gathering cattle — only the object tells you which meaning it is.

ru: злорадно напоминать; сыпать соль на рану; тыкать носом
separable: separable, and the object is almost always *it*: *rub it in*. ✗ *rub in it* is impossible
gloss: To keep mentioning something that embarrasses or upsets another person.
examples: I know I lost — don't *rub it in*.
He *rubbed* it *in* for a week.
She kept *rubbing in* how much cheaper her ticket had been.
contrast: Double the *b*: *rubbed*, *rubbing*. The literal sense splits the same way: *rub the lotion in*, *rub it in*.

ru: передаваться, передаться (кому-л.); влиять, повлиять (о привычках, настроении)
separable: inseparable — the person follows *on*: *rub off on him*, never ✗ *rub him off on*
transitivity: transitive — with *on* before the person it reaches
gloss: To pass from one person to another, of a habit, mood, or quality.
examples: Her optimism *rubs off on* everyone in the room.
Some of his bad habits have *rubbed off on* me.
You can see the coach's style *rubbing off on* the younger players.
contrast: The subject is the quality, not the person: *his calm rubbed off on me*. Without a person named, *on* drops: *I hope some of it rubs off*.

ru: исключать, исключить; отвергать, отвергнуть (как невозможное)
separable: separable — *rule out a strike*, *rule a strike out*, *rule it out*
gloss: To decide that something is impossible or will not happen.
examples: Doctors have *ruled out* anything serious.
She hasn't *ruled out* running again.
The weather *rules* a picnic *out*.
contrast: Also used of players: *he was ruled out for the season* — declared unable to play. The opposite, *rule in*, exists but is rare outside medicine.

ru: бросаться, броситься очертя голову; торопиться, поторопиться с (решением)
separable: inseparable — what you hurry into follows *into*: *rush into a contract*. With a person it becomes *rush someone into something*: *don't rush me into signing*
gloss: To do something important too quickly, without enough thought.
examples: Don't *rush into* a decision you'll regret.
They *rushed into* marriage after two months.
He's *rushing into* it because the price expires tonight.
contrast: The *-es* ending: *she rushes into things*. Almost always a warning — you rarely hear it as praise.

ru: спешно проводить, провести; протаскивать, протащить (закон); делать, сделать наспех
separable: separable when something is pushed through a process — *rush the order through*, *rush it through*; with the object after the particle it means doing something fast: *rush through dinner*
gloss: To deal with something too quickly, or to push it through a process at speed.
examples: Congress *rushed* the bill *through* before the recess.
Don't *rush through* the instructions.
They're *rushing* her *through* admissions now.
contrast: Word order carries the meaning: *rush the paperwork through* is about the process; *rush through the paperwork* is about your own haste.

ru: наспех готовить, приготовить; раздобывать, раздобыть; сообразить (на скорую руку)
separable: separable — *rustle up a meal*, *rustle a meal up*, *rustle it up*
gloss: To make or find something quickly out of whatever is available, especially food.
examples: I'll *rustle up* some sandwiches.
He *rustled up* three volunteers in an hour.
She's *rustling up* dinner from what's left in the fridge.
contrast: The *t* is silent: RUS-uhl. From cattle *rustling* — the verb keeps the sense of getting hold of something fast and informally.
